# Overview



## What is ProFOLD2?

ProFOLD2 is a PyTorch-based protein 3D structure prediction application that re-implements and extends the AlphaFold2 architecture. Developed by Chungong Yu and Dongbo Bu, it provides an end-to-end framework covering data ingestion, model training, inference, structure relaxation, and even a web interface — all within a single, modular codebase released under the MIT license. The project is designed for both research experimentation and production deployment, with built-in support for distributed multi-node training via PyTorch's distributed backend and SLURM scheduler integration.

Sources: [README.md](README.md), [setup.py](setup.py#L1-L48)

## Architecture at a Glance

ProFOLD2 follows a pipeline architecture that transforms raw protein sequences and structural data into 3D atomic coordinates. The diagram below illustrates the high-level data flow from input to output:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Input Data] --> B[Data Pipeline]
    B --> C[Feature Builder]
    C --> D[Input Embeddings]
    D --> E[Evoformer / Pairformer]
    E --> F[Task Heads]
    F --> G[Structure Module + IPA]
    G --> H[3D Coordinates]
    H --> I{Post-processing}
    I --> J[Amber Relaxation]
    I --> K[Potts Model / Sequence Design]
    J --> L[PDB Output]
    K --> L

    subgraph "Training Loop"
        T[Loss Computation] --> U[Gradient Optimization]
        U --> V[Recycling Iterations]
        V --> E
    end

    subgraph "CLI Entry Point"
        CLI["main.py"] --> CMD1["train"]
        CLI --> CMD2["predict"]
        CLI --> CMD3["evaluate"]
    end
```

The core model, `AlphaFold2`, lives in [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L128-L321) and orchestrates the entire forward pass. It accepts a feature batch, runs it through input embeddings, the Evoformer trunk, multiple task-specific heads, and optionally a structure module for 3D coordinate prediction. A recycling wrapper, `AlphaFold2WithRecycling`, iterates this process to refine predictions across multiple passes [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L323-L327).

Sources: [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L128-L321), [profold2/command/main.py](profold2/command/main.py#L26-L29)

## Project Structure

The repository is organized into clearly separated concerns. Below is the directory layout with the purpose of each module:

```
ProFOLD2/
├── main.py                  # CLI entry point (delegates to profold2.command.main)
├── install_env.sh           # Conda + pip environment setup script
├── setup.py                 # Package installation with CUDA kernel extensions
│
├── profold2/                # Core library package
│   ├── command/             # CLI subcommands: train, predict, evaluate, relax
│   ├── common/              # Protein constants, utilities, residue definitions
│   ├── data/                # Dataset loading, feature pipelines, ESM embeddings
│   ├── model/               # Neural network modules (the heart of the system)
│   │   ├── alphafold2.py    #   Main AlphaFold2 model + recycling wrapper
│   │   ├── evoformer.py     #   Evoformer and Pairformer transformer blocks
│   │   ├── folding.py       #   Structure Module with Invariant Point Attention
│   │   ├── head.py          #   15+ prediction heads (distogram, folding, etc.)
│   │   ├── features.py      #   Feature transformation functions
│   │   ├── potts.py         #   Potts model for sequence design (MCMC sampling)
│   │   ├── sequence.py      #   ESM embedding integration
│   │   ├── kernel/          #   Custom CUDA kernels (FusedEvoformer, CUTLASS)
│   │   └── accelerator.py   #   GPU/MLU distributed training utilities
│   ├── relax/               # Amber-based structure relaxation
│   ├── tools/               # Energy and sampling utilities
│   └── utils.py             # Shared utility functions
│
├── examples/                # Configuration examples and SLURM job scripts
├── tools/                   # Standalone utilities (PDB ops, TM-score, etc.)
├── tests/                   # Unit tests and benchmarks
├── docker/                  # Dockerfile for containerized deployment
└── web/                     # Flask-based web interface for prediction
```

Sources: [main.py](main.py#L1-L12), [profold2/command/main.py](profold2/command/main.py#L26-L29)

## Key Capabilities

ProFOLD2 goes well beyond a basic AlphaFold2 reimplementation. The table below summarizes the core capabilities and where they are implemented:

| Capability | Description | Key Module |
|---|---|---|
| **Structure Prediction** | Predict 3D atomic coordinates from amino acid sequences using the AlphaFold2 architecture | [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L128) |
| **Evoformer & Pairformer** | Dual-attention trunk with MSA row/column attention and pairwise attention; supports AlphaFold3-style Pairformer | [evoformer.py](profold2/model/evoformer.py#L199-L377) |
| **Structure Module (IPA)** | Iterative refinement of backbone frames using Invariant Point Attention | [folding.py](profold2/model/folding.py#L99-L213) |
| **15+ Prediction Heads** | Distogram, Folding, PLDDT, PAE, Contact, Coevolution, Pairing, TM-score, Fitness, Violation, and more | [head.py](profold2/model/head.py#L91-L1692) |
| **Sequence Design** | Potts model with Gibbs and DLMC MCMC samplers for inverse folding | [potts.py](profold2/model/potts.py#L12-L159) |
| **ESM Integration** | Pre-trained protein language model embeddings (ESM-1b, ESM-MSA1b) via Facebook Research | [sequence.py](profold2/model/sequence.py#L153-L254) |
| **Multi-Chain / Multimer** | Native support for multi-chain protein complexes with pseudo-linker augmentation | [dataset.py](profold2/data/dataset.py#L1540-L1750) |
| **Amber Relaxation** | Post-prediction structure refinement using OpenMM | [relax.py](profold2/relax/relax.py#L30-L89) |
| **Distributed Training** | Multi-node, multi-GPU training with PyTorch distributed, SLURM integration, and mixed-precision (AMP) | [trainer.py](profold2/command/trainer.py#L75-L467), [accelerator.py](profold2/model/accelerator.py#L61-L117) |
| **Custom CUDA Kernels** | CUTLASS-based fused kernels and FusedEvoformer for optimized attention | [kernel/](profold2/model/kernel/__init__.py) |
| **Web Interface** | Flask-based UI for submitting prediction jobs and browsing results | [web/app.py](web/app.py#L1-L241) |

Sources: [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L128-L321), [profold2/model/head.py](profold2/model/head.py#L91-L1692), [profold2/model/potts.py](profold2/model/potts.py#L12-L159)

## How the Model Works — A Conceptual Walkthrough

At a high level, the `AlphaFold2` class implements the following forward pass:

1. **Input Embeddings**: Raw sequence tokens, pairwise features (e.g., distance histograms), and optional template features are projected into the model's hidden dimension via the `InputEmbeddings` module. This produces MSA representations (shape `B × M × N × C_msa`) and pairwise representations (shape `B × N × N × C_pair`).

2. **Evoformer Trunk**: The Evoformer — a stack of `EvoformerBlock` layers — iteratively refines these representations through a combination of MSA attention, pairwise attention, and cross-representation transitions. It can operate in two modes: the classic AlphaFold2 mode (with full MSA) and a Pairformer mode (MSA-free, AlphaFold3-style).

3. **Single Representation Extraction**: The first row of the MSA representation is projected into a compact single representation (shape `B × N × C_single`), which serves as the primary input to all prediction heads.

4. **Task Heads**: A configurable set of prediction heads operates on the single and pairwise representations. The `HeaderBuilder` dynamically assembles heads from a JSON configuration. Each head produces predictions and, during training, computes its own loss contribution.

5. **Recycling**: The `AlphaFold2WithRecycling` wrapper iterates the forward pass multiple times, feeding recycled representations (MSA first row, pairwise features, and optionally 3D coordinates and frames) back into the model to progressively refine predictions.

Sources: [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L213-L320), [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L323-L422)

## CLI Commands

The entry point is [main.py](main.py#L1-L12), which delegates to [profold2/command/main.py](profold2/command/main.py). Three primary commands are available:

| Command | Description | Module |
|---|---|---|
| `train` | Train a model from scratch or fine-tune an existing checkpoint | [trainer.py](profold2/command/trainer.py#L75-L467) |
| `predict` | Run inference on sequences (FASTA) or preprocessed data | [predictor.py](profold2/command/predictor.py#L1-L100) |
| `evaluate` | Evaluate model predictions against ground truth structures | [evaluator.py](profold2/command/evaluator.py) |

Example usage:

```bash
# Train with default settings
python main.py train --prefix=OUTPUT_DIR

# Predict from FASTA files
python main.py predict --models model_file.pt fasta_files/*.fasta

# Show all options
python main.py train -h
```

Sources: [profold2/command/main.py](profold2/command/main.py#L26-L29), [README.md](README.md#L27-L60)

## Technology Stack

| Component | Technology | Version |
|---|---|---|
| **Language** | Python | 3.9+ (recommended 3.11) |
| **Deep Learning** | PyTorch | ≥ 2.3.1 |
| **Molecular Dynamics** | OpenMM + PDBFixer | ≥ 8.0.0 |
| **Bioinformatics** | BioPython | latest |
| **Visualization** | TensorBoard | latest |
| **Mixed Precision** | torch.amp (AMP) | built-in |
| **CUDA Kernels** | CUTLASS | submodule |
| **Container** | Docker (NVIDIA CUDA 12.1) | [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile) |

Sources: [setup.py](setup.py#L21-L27), [requirements.txt](requirements.txt#L1-L9), [install_env.sh](install_env.sh#L1-L71), [docker/Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L57)

> [!TIP]
> The project uses git submodules for optimized CUDA kernels. After cloning, run `git submodule update --init` to fetch the CUTLASS and FusedEvoformer components. Without these, the model still runs in pure PyTorch mode but at reduced performance.

> [!TIP]
> All prediction heads and their hyperparameters are defined via JSON configuration files (see [examples/model_headers_150m.json](examples/model_headers_150m.json) and [examples/model_features_150m.json](examples/model_features_150m.json)). This makes it straightforward to swap heads, adjust loss weights, or experiment with different architectures without modifying Python code.

# Quick Start



This guide walks you through installing, configuring, and running ProFOLD2 — a protein 3D structure prediction application built on the AlphaFold2 architecture — from a single-command prediction to a full multi-node training pipeline. By the end, you will have a working installation capable of predicting protein structures from FASTA sequences and a clear mental model of the system's command-line interface.

## Prerequisites

ProFOLD2 requires a CUDA-capable GPU and a specific stack of system-level and Python dependencies. The project targets **Python 3.11** and **CUDA 12.1.1** by default, with **PyTorch 2.3.1** as the deep learning runtime. The provided [install_env.sh](install_env.sh#L31-L34) codifies these version pins as shell variables, and the [setup.py](setup.py#L39) classifier enforces the Python version requirement.

| Dependency | Minimum Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.11 | Runtime environment |
| PyTorch | ≥ 2.3.1 | Model training & inference |
| CUDA Toolkit | 12.1.1 | GPU compute backend |
| GCC/G++ | 12.4.0 | Custom CUDA kernel compilation (FusedEvoformer) |
| OpenMM | ≥ 8.0.0 | Amber structure relaxation |
| BioPython | — | PDB/FASTA parsing |
| TensorBoard | — | Training metric visualization |

> [!TIP]
> If you plan to use the **FusedEvoformer** (a performance-optimized variant with custom CUDA kernels), you must initialize the `cutlass/` git submodule after cloning. This is strongly recommended for production training workloads but optional for basic inference.

## Installation

ProFOLD2 follows a clone → environment → dependencies → build workflow. The entire process is automated by the provided shell script, which handles conda package installation, PyTorch CUDA variant selection, and CUDA development library setup in the correct order.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Clone Repository"] --> B["Create Conda Env"]
    B --> C["Run install_env.sh"]
    C --> D{"Use FusedEvoformer?"}
    D -- Yes --> E["git submodule update --init"]
    D -- No --> F["Ready to Use"]
    E --> F
```

Start by cloning the repository and creating a conda environment:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bigict/ProFOLD2.git
cd ProFOLD2
git submodule update --init  # Required for FusedEvoformer; recommended
conda create -n profold2 python=3.11
conda activate profold2
bash install_env.sh
```

The [install_env.sh](install_env.sh#L1-L71) script performs dependency installation in four stages: (1) the C++ compiler toolchain via `gxx` and `ninja`, (2) OpenMM and PDBFixer from conda-forge alongside the CUDA version, (3) PyTorch with the matching CUDA variant from the official PyTorch wheel index, and (4) CUDA development libraries (`cuda-cccl`, `cuda-libraries-dev`, `cuda-nvcc`, `libcurand-dev`) required for custom kernel compilation. A `--do-cleanup` flag (`-c`) is available to purge pip and conda caches after each stage.

## Understanding the CLI Architecture

ProFOLD2 exposes a unified command-line interface through [main.py](main.py#L1-L12), which delegates to [profold2/command/main.py](profold2/command/main.py#L72-L75). The CLI is structured as a subcommand router with three primary operations, plus distributed-training infrastructure arguments that are shared across all commands.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Entry["python main.py"] --> Router["profold2/command/main.py<br/>create_args() + create_fn()"]
    Router --> SubTrain["train"]
    Router --> SubPredict["predict"]
    Router --> SubEval["evaluate"]
    
    SharedArgs["--nnodes, --node_rank,<br/>--local_rank, --init_method"]
    
    SubTrain --> WorkerModel["WorkerModel<br/>(distributed wrapper)"]
    SubPredict --> WorkerModel
    SubEval --> WorkerModel
    
    WorkerModel --> GPU["GPU Device"]
    WorkerModel --> DDP["DistributedDataParallel<br/>(if multi-node)"]
```

The [command router](profold2/command/main.py#L12-L16) registers three subcommands — `train`, `predict`, and `evaluate` — each with its own argument parser. All three share a common `-o/--prefix` argument for output directory and a `-v/--verbose` flag. Distributed arguments (`--nnodes`, `--node_rank`, `--local_rank`, `--init_method`) are parsed at the top level and consumed by the [WorkerModel](profold2/command/worker.py#L91-L94) class, which handles device placement, DDP wrapping, and SLURM environment variable auto-detection.

## Running Your First Prediction

Prediction is the fastest way to validate your installation. The `predict` subcommand accepts FASTA files as input and produces PDB structure files as output, optionally running Amber relaxation on the predicted structures.

### Minimal Prediction Command

```bash
python main.py predict \
    --prefix=./output \
    --models path/to/model.pth \
    --fasta_fmt=single \
    sequence.fasta
```

Let's break down each argument:

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--models` | (required) | Path to a trained model checkpoint. Supports `[NAME=]PATH` format for multiple models |
| `--prefix` | `.` | Output directory prefix. Results are written to `<prefix>/<protein_name>/` |
| `--fasta_fmt` | `single` | Input format: `single` (one sequence per file) or `a3m` (MSA alignment format) |
| `--fasta_files` | (positional) | One or more FASTA file paths (supports glob patterns) |
| `--model_recycles` | `0` | Number of structure recycling iterations (higher = better quality, slower) |
| `--model_shard_size` | `None` | Memory optimization: shard the evoformer computation |
| `--no_relaxer` | `false` | Skip Amber relaxation (faster output, less refined structures) |
| `--amp_enabled` | `false` | Enable automatic mixed precision for reduced GPU memory usage |

Sources: [predictor.py](profold2/command/predictor.py#L298-L358)

### Input Format Options

The predictor supports two input paradigms through the [data loader factory](profold2/command/predictor.py#L47-L94):

**FASTA files** (default): Provide individual `.fasta` files or a list file via `--fasta_file_list`. Each file is parsed into a single sequence. The `--fasta_fmt=single` mode treats each file as one sequence, while `--fasta_fmt=a3m` treats multi-sequence files as MSA alignments (with random downsampling to `--max_msa_size` if needed).

**Pre-processed dataset**: Use `--data_dir` to load from a zipped dataset directory (the same format used for training), with optional `--data_idx` for filtering and `--add_pseudo_linker` for multi-chain complex prediction.

### Output Structure

For each input sequence, the predictor creates an output directory under `<prefix>/<protein_name>/` containing:

- `unrelaxed_<model_name>.pdb` — Raw model prediction
- `relaxed_<model_name>.pdb` — Amber-relaxed structure (unless `--no_relaxer`)
- `result.json` — Ranking scores and metadata (unless `--no_pth`)

## Training a Model

Training is the most configuration-heavy workflow. At minimum, you need a training dataset, model configuration JSON files (features and headers), and sufficient GPU memory. The [examples/train.job](examples/train.job#L92-L130) script demonstrates a complete training configuration for the "150m" model variant.

### Minimal Training Command

```bash
python main.py train \
    --prefix=./output \
    --train_data=./train.zip \
    --model_features=./model_features.json \
    --model_headers=./model_headers.json \
    --model_dim 384 256 128 \
    --model_evoformer_depth 64 \
    --model_evoformer_head_num 8 \
    --model_evoformer_head_dim 32 \
    --model_evoformer_accept_msa \
    --model_recycles=2 \
    --num_batches=10000
```

### Key Training Arguments

The training command exposes a large parameter surface through [add_arguments](profold2/command/trainer.py#L471-L813). The table below groups the most important ones by category:

| Category | Argument | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Data** | `--train_data` | `train.zip` | Training dataset (zipped directory) |
| | `--train_idx` | `None` | Optional index file for data filtering |
| | `--train_data_weights` | `None` | Per-sample weighting file for biased sampling |
| | `--max_msa_size` | `1024` | Maximum MSA depth per sample |
| | `--max_var_size` | `8192` | Maximum variant depth per sample |
| **Cropping** | `--min_crop_len` | `80` | Don't crop sequences shorter than this |
| | `--max_crop_len` | `255` | Crop sequences longer than this |
| | `--crop_algorithm` | `auto` | Crop strategy: `auto`, `random`, or `knn` |
| | `--train_crop_probability` | `0.0` | Probability of applying cropping |
| **Model** | `--model_features` | `model_features_main.json` | Feature configuration JSON |
| | `--model_headers` | `model_headers_main.json` | Prediction head configuration JSON |
| | `--model_dim` | `384 256 128` | Triplet: (s_dim, z_dim, extra_dim) |
| | `--model_evoformer_depth` | `1` | Number of Evoformer blocks |
| | `--model_evoformer_accept_msa_attn` | `false` | Enable MSATransformer blocks |
| | `--model_evoformer_accept_frame_attn` | `false` | Enable FrameTransformer blocks |
| **Optimization** | `--learning_rate` | `1e-3` | Adam optimizer learning rate |
| | `--gradient_accumulate_every` | `16` | Gradient accumulation steps |
| | `--batch_size` | `1` | Samples per batch |
| **Checkpointing** | `--checkpoint_every` | `100` | Save checkpoint every N steps |
| | `--checkpoint_max_to_keep` | `5` | Maximum retained checkpoints |
| **Monitoring** | `--eval_every` | `100` | Run evaluation every N steps |
| | `--tuning_every` | `10` | Run tuning every N steps |

Sources: [trainer.py](profold2/command/trainer.py#L471-L813)

> [!TIP]
> Training progress is automatically logged to TensorBoard. Run `tensorboard --logdir=./output` and open `http://localhost:6006` to monitor loss curves, TM-score metrics, and confidence predictions in real time. The training loop uses a [cycling data iterator](profold2/command/trainer.py#L137-L146) that cycles through epochs indefinitely until `--num_batches` steps are completed.

### Model Configuration Files

Two JSON files govern model architecture: **model_features** controls which input features are computed and how (MSA processing, template embedding, etc.), while **model_headers** defines which prediction heads are active (structure folding, confidence, fitness/variant prediction, coevolution). Example files are provided in [examples/](examples/model_features_150m.json) for the "150m" model variant. These files are loaded during [training initialization](profold2/command/trainer.py#L84-L84) and passed to the `FeatureBuilder` and model constructor.

## Evaluating a Model

The `evaluate` subcommand runs a trained model against a held-out test dataset, computing structural metrics including **TM-score** (via Kabsch alignment) and per-head losses. It requires a pre-trained checkpoint and a test dataset.

```bash
python main.py evaluate \
    --prefix=./eval_output \
    --model=path/to/model.pth \
    --eval_data=./test.zip \
    --crop_probability=0 \
    --min_crop_len=256 \
    --max_crop_len=256 \
    --model_recycles=2
```

The [evaluation loop](profold2/command/evaluator.py#L180-L198) iterates through the test dataset, running inference with `torch.no_grad()` and computing metrics against ground-truth coordinates when available. Results are logged per-sample and aggregated. When fitness/variant heads are configured, evaluation also outputs `.pkl` files containing variant predictions, coevolution weights, and gating values.

## Monitoring and Visualization

ProFOLD2 integrates two monitoring backends accessible during training:

**TensorBoard** is the primary metric visualization tool. The training function creates a [SummaryWriter](profold2/command/trainer.py#L270-L271) that logs per-head losses under `Loss/train@<head_name>` and evaluation metrics under corresponding eval prefixes. Launch with:

```bash
tensorboard --logdir=./output/runs
```

**Weights & Biases** (optional) can be enabled via `--wandb_enabled`, `--wandb_project`, `--wandb_name`, and `--wandb_mode=offline|online`. The [wandb_setup](profold2/command/trainer.py#L33-L45) function initializes the W&B run and logs both hyperparameters and per-step loss values.

## Running on a SLURM Cluster

ProFOLD2 provides production-ready [SLURM job scripts](examples/README.md#L7-L21) in the `examples/` directory. Each script supports both SLURM and local execution via the `-p {slurm,local}` flag:

```bash
# SLURM cluster
sbatch -D . -p <partition> examples/predict.job -- --verbose sequence.fasta

# Local machine (single node)
bash examples/predict.job -p local -- --verbose sequence.fasta
```

The job scripts handle distributed environment setup automatically: they detect SLURM node lists, derive the master address for NCCL initialization, set environment variables (`NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY=AF_INET`, `NCCL_TIMEOUT=3600`), and activate the conda environment. The [distributed worker](profold2/command/worker.py#L222-L266) reads `SLURM_NNODES`, `SLURM_NODEID`, and `LOCAL_RANK` environment variables to configure PyTorch's process group without manual intervention.

Sources: [train.job](examples/train.job#L47-L63), [predict.job](examples/predict.job#L47-L63), [evaluate.job](examples/evaluate.job#L47-L63)

# Docker Deployment



ProFOLD2 provides a fully containerized deployment path that eliminates the need to manually configure CUDA toolchains, conda environments, or bioinformatics dependencies. This page walks you through every layer of the Docker setup — from how the image is assembled, to how volumes are mounted, to how prediction jobs are orchestrated at runtime. By the end, you will be able to build the image, launch a prediction container, and interpret the mounting and execution model without surprises.

## Architecture Overview

The Docker deployment system consists of three cooperating components: the **Dockerfile** that builds a self-contained GPU runtime image, the **`run_docker.py`** launch script that translates host-side arguments into container invocations, and the **`predict.job`** entrypoint inside the container that actually executes ProFOLD2's prediction pipeline. Understanding how these layers connect is the key to customizing and troubleshooting your deployments.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Host["Host Machine"]
        A["run_docker.py<br/>Python launch script"] --> B["Docker Engine<br/>nvidia runtime"]
        C["FASTA files<br/>- read-only"]
        D["Data directory<br/>with model weights<br/>- read-only"]
        E["Output directory<br/>- read-write"]
        F["Torch extensions cache<br/>- read-write"]
    end

    subgraph Container["Docker Container: profold2"]
        G["/app/run_profold.sh<br/>ENTRYPOINT script"]
        H["ldconfig"]
        I["examples/predict.job<br/>--platform=local"]
        J["main.py predict<br/>PyTorch inference"]
    end

    A -->|"docker.containers.run()"| B
    B -->|"mount binds"| G
    C -->|"/mnt/fasta_path_N"| I
    D -->|"/mnt/data"| I
    E -->|"/mnt/output"| J
    F -->|"/mnt/.cache/<br/>torch_extensions_path"| J
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J
```

The diagram above shows the full lifecycle: `run_docker.py` on the host constructs bind-mounts for your data and output directories, launches the container with the `nvidia` runtime, and streams logs back to your terminal. Inside the container, a small shell wrapper calls `ldconfig` (to make GPU libraries visible, a known NVIDIA Docker quirk) and then hands off to [predict.job](examples/predict.job) in local mode.

Sources: [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L57), [run_docker.py](docker/run_docker.py#L29-L101), [predict.job](examples/predict.job#L1-L94)

## Prerequisites

Before building or running the Docker image, ensure your host system meets the following requirements:

| Requirement | Minimum Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA Driver | 525+ (Linux) | GPU compute support |
| NVIDIA Container Toolkit | ≥ 1.14 | `--runtime=nvidia` support |
| Docker Engine | ≥ 24.0 | Build and run containers |
| Python | 3.9+ | For `run_docker.py` launcher only |
| Docker SDK for Python | latest | `pip install docker` |
| Disk Space | ~15 GB | Image build + CUDA toolchain |
| CUDA Version | 12.1.1 | Match the default `ARG` in Dockerfile |

Verify your NVIDIA Container Toolkit is working:

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi
```

If you see a GPU listing, your runtime is correctly configured.

Sources: [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L5), [requirements.txt](docker/requirements.txt#L1-L3)

## Building the Docker Image

The Dockerfile lives at [`docker/Dockerfile`](docker/Dockerfile) and is designed to be built from the **project root directory** — this is critical because it uses `COPY . ${profold_home}` to transfer the entire repository into the image at line 35. The base image is `nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04`, selected via a build argument so you can swap CUDA versions if needed.

### Build Steps

```bash
# From the project root directory
cd ProFOLD2
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t profold2 .
```

To build with a different CUDA version:

```bash
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile --build-arg CUDA=12.4.0 -t profold2:cu124 .
```

### What Happens During the Build

The build process executes these stages sequentially:

1. **System packages** — installs `cuda-command-line-tools`, `hmmer`, `kalign`, `tzdata`, and `wget` via `apt-get` ([Dockerfile#L12-L18](docker/Dockerfile#L12-L18)). HMMER and Kalign are bioinformatics tools used by AlphaFold-style pipelines for sequence alignment.
2. **Miniconda** — downloads and installs Miniconda3 into `/opt/conda`, then adds it to `PATH` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` ([Dockerfile#L21-L31](docker/Dockerfile#L21-L31)).
3. **Project copy** — the entire repository is copied into `/app/profold2` ([Dockerfile#L34-L35](docker/Dockerfile#L34-L35)).
4. **Dependency installation** — runs [`install_env.sh -c`](install_env.sh) inside the container. The `-c` flag triggers cache cleanup after each conda/pip stage to minimize layer size ([Dockerfile#L38-L39](docker/Dockerfile#L38-L39)).
5. **ldconfig permission** — sets the SETUID bit on `/sbin/ldconfig.real` so that non-root users inside the container can run it ([Dockerfile#L42-L42](docker/Dockerfile#L42-L42)).
6. **Entrypoint script** — creates `/app/run_profold.sh`, a thin wrapper that calls `ldconfig` and then invokes `examples/predict.job` with all forwarded arguments ([Dockerfile#L50-L56](docker/Dockerfile#L50-L56)).

> [!TIP]
> The build context must be the **project root**, not the `docker/` directory. The Dockerfile references `install_env.sh` and `examples/predict.job` using paths relative to the build context. Running `docker build -f docker/Dockerfile .` from the root is the only supported approach.

Sources: [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L57), [install_env.sh](install_env.sh#L1-L71)

## Dependency Stack Inside the Image

The [`install_env.sh`](install_env.sh) script orchestrates a layered dependency installation. Here is the complete stack with versions, exactly as configured in the build:

| Layer | Package(s) | Version | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| C++ Compiler | `gxx`, `ninja` | GCC 12.4.0 | conda-forge |
| Molecular Dynamics | `openmm`, `pdbfixer` | 8.0.0 | conda-forge |
| CUDA Runtime | `cuda-version`, `cuda-cccl`, `cuda-libraries-dev`, `cuda-nvcc`, `libcurand-dev` | 12.1 | nvidia channels |
| Deep Learning | `torch` | 2.3.1+cu121 | PyPI (with CUDA index) |
| Bioinformatics | `biopython`, `einops` | latest | conda-forge |
| Monitoring | `tensorboard`, `tqdm` | latest | conda-forge |

The script uses `cleanup()` function calls between each installation stage to purge pip and conda caches, keeping the final image as compact as possible ([install_env.sh#L24-L29](install_env.sh#L24-L29)). All versions are controlled by environment variables at the top of the script (lines 31-34), making them straightforward to override.

Sources: [install_env.sh](install_env.sh#L31-L71)

## Running Predictions with `run_docker.py`

The recommended way to launch ProFOLD2 inside Docker is via [`docker/run_docker.py`](docker/run_docker.py), a Python script that handles volume mounting, GPU configuration, and container lifecycle. It requires only the `docker` Python package ([docker/requirements.txt](docker/requirements.txt#L1-L3)).

### Basic Usage

```bash
python docker/run_docker.py \
    --data_dir /path/to/model_weights \
    --models model_150m \
    --output_dir /tmp/profold_output \
    protein1.fasta protein2.fasta
```

### Complete Command-Line Reference

The script exposes these arguments ([run_docker.py#L103-L142](docker/run_docker.py#L103-L142)):

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--docker_image_name` | str | `profold2` | Name of the pre-built Docker image |
| `--gpu_list` | list | `all` | Specific GPU IDs to expose (e.g., `0 1`) |
| `--output_dir` | str | `/tmp/profold` | Host directory for prediction results |
| `--data_dir` | str | `None` | Host directory containing model weights |
| `--models` | list | — | Model files (names or paths, `.pth` auto-appended) |
| `--model_recycles` | int | `2` | Number of structure recycles in inference |
| `--model_shard_size` | int | `256` | Shard size for the Evoformer model |
| `--add_pseudo_linker` | flag | off | Enable loading protein complex data |
| `--no_relaxer` | flag | off | Skip AMBER relaxation of predicted structures |
| `--no_gpu_relax` | flag | off | Run AMBER relaxation on CPU instead of GPU |
| `fasta_files` | list | — (required) | One or more FASTA files to predict |
| `-v, --verbose` | flag | off | Enable debug-level logging |

### How Volume Mounting Works

The launcher creates four categories of bind-mounts, each with a specific purpose ([run_docker.py#L13-L76](docker/run_docker.py#L13-L76)):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Host["Host Filesystem"]
        A["/path/to/models/"] -->|read-only| B["/mnt/data/"]
        C["protein.fasta"] -->|read-only| D["/mnt/fasta_path_0/"]
        E["/tmp/profold_output/"] -->|read-write| F["/mnt/output/"]
        G["~/.cache/torch_extensions_profold2/"] -->|read-write| H["/mnt/.cache/torch_extensions_path/"]
    end
```

| Mount | Host Source | Container Target | Mode | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Data directory | `--data_dir` | `/mnt/data/` | read-only | Model weights and datasets |
| FASTA files | positional args | `/mnt/fasta_path_N/` | read-only | Input sequences (one mount per file) |
| Output directory | `--output_dir` | `/mnt/output/` | read-write | Prediction results (PDB files, metrics) |
| Torch extensions | `~/.cache/torch_extensions_profold2/` | `/mnt/.cache/torch_extensions_path/` | read-write | JIT-compiled CUDA kernels |

The torch extensions cache is **read-write** because PyTorch compiles custom CUDA kernels on first use and caches them for subsequent runs. By mounting this directory out of the container, you avoid recompilation on every launch ([run_docker.py#L49-L54](docker/run_docker.py#L49-L54)).

### GPU Configuration

GPU visibility is controlled via the `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` environment variable, which the launcher sets from `--gpu_list` ([run_docker.py#L90-L90](docker/run_docker.py#L90-L90)). The container uses the `nvidia` runtime ([run_docker.py#L84-L84](docker/run_docker.py#L84-L84)), which is essential for CUDA access.

```bash
# Use specific GPUs
python docker/run_docker.py --gpu_list 0 2 --data_dir ... model1.fasta

# Use all available GPUs (default)
python docker/run_docker.py --data_dir ... model1.fasta
```

### Container Isolation and Permissions

The container runs with the **same UID and GID as your host user** ([run_docker.py#L88-L88](docker/run_docker.py#L88-L88)), which means output files are written with your ownership — no root permission issues. The container is configured with `remove=True` ([run_docker.py#L85-L85](docker/run_docker.py#L85-L85)), so it cleans itself up after execution. A signal handler catches `SIGINT` (Ctrl+C) and kills the container gracefully ([run_docker.py#L97-L97](docker/run_docker.py#L97-L97)).

Sources: [run_docker.py](docker/run_docker.py#L1-L147)

## Understanding the Container Entrypoint

When the container starts, it executes `/app/run_profold.sh` ([Dockerfile#L56-L56](docker/Dockerfile#L56-L56)). This script, generated at build time, does two things:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
cd /app/profold2
ldconfig
/app/profold2/examples/predict.job "$@"
```

The `ldconfig` call resolves a known NVIDIA Docker issue where GPU devices are not visible until shared library caches are refreshed ([nvidia-docker#1399](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-docker/issues/1399)). The `ldconfig` binary has its SETUID bit set during the build ([Dockerfile#L42-L42](docker/Dockerfile#L42-L42)), enabling it to run as non-root.

The `predict.job` script then runs with `--platform=local` (passed as the first argument by `run_docker.py` at [line 30](docker/run_docker.py#L30-L30)), which tells it to bypass SLURM scheduling and execute directly. Inside the script, it activates the conda environment and invokes:

```bash
python /app/profold2/main.py predict \
    --platform=local \
    -- \
    --map_location=cpu \
    --models /mnt/data/model_150m.pth \
    --prefix=/mnt/output \
    --model_recycles=2 \
    --model_shard_size=256 \
    /mnt/fasta_path_0/protein.fasta
```

The `--map_location=cpu` argument ([run_docker.py#L32-L32](docker/run_docker.py#L32-L32)) ensures that model weights are loaded into CPU memory first before being transferred to GPU, preventing OOM errors during weight loading.

Sources: [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L50-L56), [predict.job](examples/predict.job#L84-L93), [run_docker.py](docker/run_docker.py#L30-L76)

## Step-by-Step Deployment Walkthrough

This flowchart captures the complete end-to-end process from cloning the repository to receiving prediction results:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["1. Clone repository"] --> B["2. Build Docker image<br/>docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t profold2 ."]
    B --> C{"3. Prepare data"}
    C --> C1["Download model weights<br/>(e.g., model_150m.pth)"]
    C --> C2["Prepare FASTA files<br/>with protein sequences"]
    C1 --> D["4. Organize host directories"]
    C2 --> D
    D --> E["5. Launch container<br/>python docker/run_docker.py --data_dir ./models --models model_150m --output_dir ./results protein.fasta"]
    E --> F["6. Monitor logs<br/>(streamed in real-time)"]
    F --> G["7. Collect results<br/>from --output_dir"]
```

### Concrete Example: Predicting a Single Protein

Assuming you have cloned the repository and placed your model weights and FASTA file:

```bash
# Directory structure on the host
# /home/user/profold2_run/
# ├── models/
# │   └── model_150m.pth          # Pre-trained model weights
# └── input/
#     └── 1CRN.fasta              # Protein sequence file

# Build the image (one-time, from project root)
cd ProFOLD2
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t profold2 .

# Run prediction
python docker/run_docker.py \
    --docker_image_name profold2 \
    --data_dir /home/user/profold2_run/models \
    --models model_150m \
    --model_recycles 3 \
    --model_shard_size 256 \
    --output_dir /home/user/profold2_run/results \
    /home/user/profold2_run/input/1CRN.fasta
```

### Example: Batch Prediction with Multiple Proteins

```bash
python docker/run_docker.py \
    --data_dir /home/user/profold2_run/models \
    --models model_150m \
    --output_dir /home/user/profold2_run/results \
    --no_relaxer \
    --verbose \
    /home/user/profold2_run/input/protein_A.fasta \
    /home/user/profold2_run/input/protein_B.fasta \
    /home/user/profold2_run/input/protein_C.fasta
```

### Example: Using Specific GPUs

```bash
python docker/run_docker.py \
    --gpu_list 0 1 \
    --data_dir /home/user/profold2_run/models \
    --models model_150m \
    --output_dir /home/user/profold2_run/results \
    /home/user/profold2_run/input/1CRN.fasta
```

Sources: [run_docker.py](docker/run_docker.py#L103-L147), [predict.job](examples/predict.job#L84-L93)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `Could not select GPU device` | NVIDIA Container Toolkit not installed or `nvidia` runtime unavailable | Install [NVIDIA Container Toolkit](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/latest/install-guide.html) and verify with `docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi` |
| `Permission denied` on output files | Container writes as root (UID mismatch) | The launcher maps your UID/GID by default. If running raw `docker run`, add `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)` |
| `Failed to find source directory to mount` | FASTA or data path doesn't exist on host | Verify all paths with `ls` before passing them to `run_docker.py` |
| Slow first run, then fast | CUDA kernel JIT compilation | Normal behavior. Torch extensions are cached in `~/.cache/torch_extensions_profold2/` after first run |
| `ldconfig` permission error inside container | Older Dockerfile without SETUID bit | Rebuild the image — the current Dockerfile sets `chmod u+s /sbin/ldconfig.real` |
| Model weights not found | `--models` path mismatch | When using `--models model_name` (without path), the launcher looks in `{data_target_path}/model_name.pth` ([run_docker.py#L41-L44](docker/run_docker.py#L41-L44)) |

> [!TIP]
> If you encounter CUDA version mismatches between your host driver and the container's CUDA toolkit, override the build argument: `docker build --build-arg CUDA=12.4.0 -f docker/Dockerfile -t profold2 .`. The `install_env.sh` script automatically extracts the major.minor CUDA version for dependency resolution at [line 35](install_env.sh#L35-L35).

Sources: [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L41-L46), [install_env.sh](install_env.sh#L35-L35), [run_docker.py](docker/run_docker.py#L41-L44)

## File Structure Summary

Here is the complete layout of Docker-related files within the repository, annotated with their roles:

```
ProFOLD2/
├── docker/
│   ├── Dockerfile              # Image definition (CUDA 12.1.1 + cuDNN 8)
│   ├── requirements.txt        # Host-side: just 'docker' Python package
│   └── run_docker.py           # Container orchestration launcher
├── install_env.sh              # Shared by Docker & bare-metal installation
├── examples/
│   ├── predict.job             # Container entrypoint (also used via SLURM)
│   ├── train.job               # SLURM-only (not exposed via Docker)
│   └── evaluate.job            # SLURM-only (not exposed via Docker)
├── main.py                     # CLI entry point (train/evaluate/predict)
└── requirements.txt            # Bare-metal Python dependencies
```

Note that the Docker entrypoint is wired specifically to [`predict.job`](examples/predict.job), meaning the current Docker setup is optimized for **inference only**. Training and evaluation require SLURM scheduling or manual local execution — see [CLI Command Reference](21-cli-command-reference) for those workflows.

Sources: [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L57), [run_docker.py](docker/run_docker.py#L1-L147), [predict.job](examples/predict.job#L84-L93)

# Architecture Overview



ProFOLD2 is a PyTorch-based protein 3D structure prediction framework built upon the AlphaFold2 paradigm, extended with multi-task heads, Potts model-based sequence design, distributed training infrastructure, and a web interface for interactive prediction. This page maps the high-level architecture, module responsibilities, and data flow that power the entire system.

## System Architecture

The architecture follows a layered design: a CLI entry point dispatches to domain-specific command handlers, each orchestrating a data pipeline, a model inference/training loop, and post-processing. The core neural architecture — `AlphaFold2WithRecycling` — sits at the center, wrapped by distributed training utilities and surrounded by task-specific prediction heads.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Entry["Entry Points"]
        CLI["main.py<br/>CLI (profold2)"]
        Web["web/app.py<br/>Web Interface"]
        Docker["docker/Dockerfile<br/>Container"]
    end

    subgraph CommandLayer["Command Layer (profold2/command/)"]
        Trainer["trainer.py<br/>Distributed Training"]
        Predictor["predictor.py<br/>Inference"]
        Evaluator["evaluator.py<br/>Evaluation"]
        Relaxer["relaxer.py<br/>Structure Relaxation"]
        Worker["worker.py<br/>Distributed Wrapper"]
    end

    subgraph ModelCore["Model Core (profold2/model/)"]
        AF2Recycle["AlphaFold2WithRecycling<br/>Recycling Loop"]
        AF2["AlphaFold2<br/>Main Network"]
        InputEmb["InputEmbeddings<br/>Token + Pair Embedding"]
        EvoformerStack["Evoformer<br/>48-layer Trunk"]
        PairformerStack["Pairformer<br/>Pair-only Trunk"]
        StructureMod["StructureModule<br/>IPA + Angle Prediction"]
        TemplateEmb["TemplateEmbedding<br/>Template Processing"]
        Kernel["kernel/<br/>CUTLASS Attention Kernels"]
    end

    subgraph Heads["Prediction Heads (profold2/model/head.py)"]
        FoldingHead["FoldingHead<br/>3D Structure"]
        DistHead["DistogramHead<br/>Distance Map"]
        PLDDTHead["PLDDTHead<br/>Per-residue Confidence"]
        PAEHead["PAEHead<br/>Aligned Error"]
        FitnessHead["FitnessHead<br/>Variant Fitness"]
        ContactHead["ContactHead<br/>Contact Map"]
        OtherHeads["Coevolution · Pairing · TM-score<br/>Violation · Profile · Roberta"]
    end

    subgraph DataLayer["Data Pipeline (profold2/data/)"]
        Dataset["dataset.py<br/>ProteinSequenceDataset<br/>ProteinStructureDataset"]
        Pipeline["pipeline.py<br/>DataPipeline<br/>MSA & Template Tools"]
        Features["features.py<br/>FeatureBuilder"]
        ESM["esm.py<br/>ESM Embedding"]
    end

    subgraph AdvancedModules["Advanced Modules"]
        Potts["potts.py / sampler.py<br/>Potts Model & MCMC"]
        Complexity["complexity.py<br/>Sequence Complexity"]
        Functional["functional.py<br/>FAPE, LDDT, Kabsch,<br/>Rigid Transforms"]
        Relax["relax/<br/>Amber Minimization"]
    end

    CLI --> CommandLayer
    Web --> Predictor
    Docker --> CLI

    Trainer --> Worker
    Predictor --> Worker
    Evaluator --> Worker
    Worker --> AF2Recycle

    AF2Recycle --> AF2
    AF2 --> InputEmb
    AF2 --> EvoformerStack

    AF2 --> StructureMod
    AF2 --> TemplateEmb
    AF2 --> Heads
    EvoformerStack --> Kernel

    Predictor --> DataLayer
    Predictor --> Relax
    Functional --> StructureMod

```

## Package Structure

The `profold2/` package is organized into five logical domains, each mapped to a specific concern in the prediction pipeline.

| Package | Responsibility | Key Files |
|---------|---------------|-----------|
| `profold2/command/` | CLI dispatch, distributed orchestration | `main.py`, `trainer.py`, `predictor.py`, `evaluator.py`, `worker.py`, `relaxer.py` |
| `profold2/model/` | Neural network architecture, loss functions, geometry | `alphafold2.py`, `evoformer.py`, `folding.py`, `head.py`, `functional.py`, `potts.py` |
| `profold2/data/` | Dataset loading, MSA processing, feature engineering | `dataset.py`, `pipeline.py`, `features.py` (via FeatureBuilder) |
| `profold2/common/` | Protein constants, residue type definitions | `protein.py`, `residue_constants.py` |
| `profold2/relax/` | Amber-based structure relaxation | `relax.py`, `amber_minimize.py`, `cleanup.py` |

Supporting tooling lives in `tools/` (PDB manipulation, dataset construction, TM-score calculation), `tests/` (unit and benchmark tests), and `web/` (Flask-based prediction server).

Sources: [setup.py](setup.py#L8-L47), [profold2/command/main.py](profold2/command/main.py#L12-L66)

## CLI Entry Point and Command Dispatch

The root `main.py` delegates immediately to `profold2.command.main:main`, which registers three subcommands — `train`, `evaluate`, and `predict` — each backed by a dedicated function and argument parser. Every command passes through `worker.main()`, which initializes the distributed environment (via PyTorch `DistributedDataParallel`) before invoking the actual work function on each rank.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["main.py"] --> B["command/main.py<br/>create_args()"]
    B --> C{command?}
    C -->|train| D["trainer.train()"]
    C -->|evaluate| E["evaluator.evaluate()"]
    C -->|predict| F["predictor.predict()"]
    D --> G["worker.main()"]
    E --> G
    F --> G
    G --> H["WorkerModel<br/>DDP Wrapper"]
    G --> I["WorkerFunction<br/>Rank Dispatch"]
```

The `WorkerModel` class handles model wrapping with `DistributedDataParallel`, weight loading with legacy key remapping hooks, and checkpoint serialization. It is the single point of truth for device placement and distributed model lifecycle management. The `WorkerFunction` wraps the rank-aware work function and integrates with `WorkerLogging` for rank-filtered log output.

Sources: [profold2/command/main.py](profold2/command/main.py#L19-L80), [profold2/command/worker.py](profold2/command/worker.py#L91-L186)

## Core Model Architecture

The neural model centers on two classes: `AlphaFold2` (the single-pass network) and `AlphaFold2WithRecycling` (the recycling wrapper). The recycling wrapper runs the core network multiple times under `torch.no_grad()`, feeding outputs back as `Recyclables` (MSA first-row representation, pairwise representation, coordinates, and optionally frames) before a final training-enabled pass that computes losses.

The `AlphaFold2` constructor accepts a 3-tuple `dim = (dim_single, dim_msa, dim_pairwise)` controlling the representation dimensions throughout the network. Its `forward` pass follows this sequence:

1. **Input Embedding** — `InputEmbeddings` produces MSA embeddings (`m`) and pairwise embeddings (`x`) from sequence features, residue indices, chain color/entity/symmetry tokens, and optional MSA features.
2. **Recycling Injection** — If `Recyclables` are present, pairwise distograms from previous-cycle coordinates and normalized MSA/pair representations are injected via additive connections.
3. **Evoformer Trunk** — A configurable-depth stack of `EvoformerBlock` layers iteratively refines the MSA representation `m`, pairwise representation `x`, and structural frames `t`.
4. **Single Representation Extraction** — The first row of the MSA output is projected to `dim_single` via a linear layer.
5. **Prediction Heads** — The `HeaderBuilder` dynamically instantiates heads from a declarative configuration list, each receiving the shared representation dictionary and batch.

> [!TIP]
> The model supports two distinct trunk variants: **Evoformer** (MSA + pairwise co-evolution, AlphaFold2-style) and **Pairformer** (pairwise-only, AlphaFold3-style). This is controlled by the `evoformer_depth` parameter — setting it to 0 disables the Evoformer, allowing the `Pairformer` block to operate on single/pair representations alone. The `accept_frame_attn` and `accept_frame_update` flags further extend the trunk with 3D-aware frame attention blocks.

Sources: [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L128-L322), [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L323-L422)

## Evoformer and Structure Module

Each `EvoformerBlock` interleaves three attention operations — **MSA attention** (rows attend over columns using pairwise bias), **pairwise attention** (outer product mean pooling from MSA to pairs), and optionally **frame attention** (3D frame-conditioned attention) — with corresponding feedforward transitions. The blocks operate in a configurable checkpoint segmentation mode to trade compute for memory.

The `StructureModule` implements the Invariant Point Attention (IPA) mechanism: it iteratively refines rotation quaternions and translations using equivariant transformer blocks, then decodes torsion angles via `AngleNet` to produce all-atom coordinates. A critical design choice is that rotations are detached between IPA iterations (except the last) to stabilize training, and the entire structure module runs in `float32` regardless of the upstream precision.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Evoformer["Evoformer Block × N"]
        MSAAttn["MSA Attention<br/>(row-wise, pair-biased)"]
        MSAFF["MSA FeedForward"]
        PairAttn["Pairwise Attention<br/>(outer-mean from MSA)"]
        PairFF["Pairwise FeedForward"]
        FrameAttn["Frame Attention<br/>(optional, 3D-aware)"]
        FrameUpdate["Frame Updater<br/>(optional)"]
    end

    subgraph StructMod["Structure Module"]
        IPA["IPA Block × K<br/>(equivariant)"]
        AffineUpd["Affine Update<br/>(quaternion + translation)"]
        AngleNet["AngleNet<br/>(torsion prediction)"]
        Coords["rigids_to_positions<br/>(→ all-atom coords)"]
    end

    MSAAttn --> MSAFF --> PairAttn --> PairFF
    FrameAttn --> FrameUpdate
    PairFF -->|"single repr"| IPA
    IPA --> AffineUpd --> AngleNet --> Coords
```

Sources: [profold2/model/evoformer.py](profold2/model/evoformer.py#L199-L306), [profold2/model/folding.py](profold2/model/folding.py#L99-L216)

## Prediction Head System

The `HeaderBuilder` registry maps string names to head classes, allowing the model configuration to declaratively specify which prediction tasks to enable. Each head receives a shared `representations` dictionary (containing `single`, `pair`, `msa`, and `frames`) and a `batch` dictionary (containing ground truth and masks), and optionally returns computed losses weighted by per-head configuration.

| Head | Purpose | Key Dimensions |
|------|---------|----------------|
| `FoldingHead` | 3D coordinate prediction via StructureModule + FAPE loss | `structure_module_depth`, `structure_module_heads` |
| `DistogramHead` | Pairwise distance histogram classification | `buckets_first_break`, `buckets_last_break`, `buckets_num` |
| `PLDDTHead` | Per-residue confidence (pLDDT) via binned distance error | `buckets_num`, `max_resolution` |
| `PAEHead` | Predicted aligned error for inter-chain assessment | `buckets_num`, `buckets_first_break`, `buckets_last_break` |
| `ConfidenceHead` | Aggregate confidence score | single scalar |
| `ContactHead` | Binary contact map prediction | `cutoff`, `diagonal` |
| `CoevolutionHead` | MSA co-evolution / residue recovery | `num_states`, `gating`, `apc` |
| `FitnessHead` | Variant fitness prediction (multi-task) | `task_num`, `task_weight`, `shard_size` |
| `PairingHead` | Nucleic acid base pairing prediction | `alpha`, `focal_loss` |
| `SequenceProfileHead` | Sequence profile prediction | `input_dim`, `single_repr` |
| `TMscoreHead` | TM-score prediction | `num_atoms` |
| `ViolationHead` | Structure violation penalty | — |
| `RobertaLMHead` | Masked language modeling | — |
| `MetricDictHead` | Composite evaluation metrics | — |

The head system is designed so that a single model configuration can support multiple simultaneous objectives — for example, jointly training on structure prediction (FoldingHead), distogram prediction (DistogramHead), and variant fitness prediction (FitnessHead) with independent loss weighting.

Sources: [profold2/model/head.py](profold2/model/head.py#L1662-L1692), [profold2/model/head.py](profold2/model/head.py#L91-L1065)

## Data Pipeline Architecture

The data layer provides two primary dataset classes. `ProteinStructureDataset` loads protein structures from filesystems or FoldComp databases, supporting both monomer and multimer inputs with configurable cropping algorithms (random, spatial-interface-aware), MSA depth sampling, and variant feature construction. `ProteinSequenceDataset` provides a simpler sequence-only loader for inference scenarios.

Feature engineering is handled by the `FeatureBuilder` class, which chains composable feature functions (registered via the `@take1st` decorator pattern) into a single callable pipeline. Feature functions cover sequence masking, coordinate processing, pseudo-beta construction, backbone affine frames, torsion angle computation, ESM embedding injection, and device transfer. The `DataPipeline` class orchestrates external alignment tools (JackHMMER, HHblits, HHsearch) against biological databases (UniRef90, MGNIFY, BFD, PDB70) for MSA and template generation.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Input["Data Sources"]
        PDB["PDB / mmCIF<br/>Files"]
        FoldComp["FoldComp<br/>Databases"]
        FASTA["FASTA<br/>Sequences"]
        AlignDB["UniRef90 / MGNIFY<br/>BFD / PDB70"]
    end

    subgraph Loading["Dataset Layer"]
        PSD["ProteinStructureDataset"]
        PSQD["ProteinSequenceDataset"]
        DP["DataPipeline<br/>(MSA + Templates)"]
    end

    subgraph FeatEng["Feature Engineering"]
        FB["FeatureBuilder<br/>(composable pipeline)"]
        SeqMask["seq_mask"]
        CoordMask["coord_mask"]
        PseudoBeta["pseudo_beta"]
        Affine["backbone_affine"]
        Torsion["torsion_angles"]
        ESME["esm_embedd"]
    end

    subgraph Output["Batch Tensors"]
        Batch["batch dict<br/>seq, mask, target_feat,<br/>msa_feat, coord, ..."]
    end

    PDB --> PSD
    FoldComp --> PSD
    FASTA --> PSQD
    FASTA --> DP
    AlignDB --> DP

    PSD --> FB
    PSQD --> FB
    DP --> FB

    FB --> SeqMask["seq_mask"] --> CoordMask["coord_mask"] --> PseudoBeta["pseudo_beta"] --> Affine["backbone_affine"] --> Torsion["torsion_angles"] --> ESME["esm_embedd"] --> Batch["batch dict<br/>seq, mask, target_feat,<br/>msa_feat, coord, ..."]
```

Sources: [profold2/data/dataset.py](profold2/data/dataset.py#L1165-L1252), [profold2/model/features.py](profold2/model/features.py#L19-L375), [profold2/data/pipeline.py](profold2/data/pipeline.py#L83-L124)

## Computational Infrastructure

ProFOLD2 includes two layers of performance optimization. At the **kernel level**, the `profold2/model/kernel/` package ships custom CUTLASS-based CUDA attention kernels (`attention.cpp`, `attention_cu.cu`, `attention_back.cu`) for memory-efficient Evoformer attention. The `evoformer_attn.py` module provides the Python interface to these fused kernels. At the **memory level**, `profold2/model/snapshot.py` implements a `memory_snapshot` context manager wrapping PyTorch's memory snapshot API for peak memory tracing during long training runs.

Distributed training uses PyTorch native `DistributedDataParallel` with static graph mode (`_set_static_graph()`), supporting multi-node SLURM-managed clusters via environment variables (`SLURM_NNODES`, `SLURM_NODEID`, `LOCAL_RANK`). The `no_sync_ctx` context manager conditionally disables gradient synchronization for gradient accumulation scenarios.

> [!TIP]
> The `profold2_relative_pos_s_max` and `profold2_evoformer_checkpoint_segment_size` environment variables control relative positional encoding maximum sequence-entity distance and gradient checkpointing granularity respectively, allowing runtime tuning without code changes.

Sources: [profold2/command/worker.py](profold2/command/worker.py#L134-L145), [profold2/model/alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L139-L140)

## End-to-End Data Flow

Putting all layers together, a typical training iteration proceeds as follows: the `ProteinStructureDataset` yields a raw feature dictionary, `FeatureBuilder` transforms it into model-ready tensors, `AlphaFold2WithRecycling` runs multiple inference-only recycling passes followed by one training pass, prediction heads compute forward outputs and losses, and the weighted total loss is backpropagated through the distributed model. For prediction, the flow is similar but skips loss computation and optionally runs Amber relaxation as a post-processing step.

| Stage | Component | Key Output |
|-------|-----------|------------|
| Data Loading | `ProteinStructureDataset` | Raw feature dict (seq, coord, msa) |
| Feature Engineering | `FeatureBuilder` | Model tensors (target_feat, mask, emb_seq, ...) |
| Model Forward | `AlphaFold2WithRecycling` | Headers dict with predictions + total loss |
| Post-Processing | `relax/` (prediction only) | Energy-minimized PDB structures |

Sources: [profold2/command/trainer.py](profold2/command/trainer.py#L75-L468), [profold2/command/predictor.py](profold2/command/predictor.py#L131-L298)

This overview has mapped the structural skeleton of ProFOLD2. The following pages provide progressively deeper dives into specific subsystems:

- **[AlphaFold2 Core Pipeline](5-alphafold2-core-pipeline)** — Detailed walkthrough of the `AlphaFold2.forward()` data flow from input embedding to head outputs
- **[Evoformer and Pairformer Blocks](6-evoformer-and-pairformer-blocks)** — Attention mechanisms, triangular multiplicative updates, and the two trunk variants
- **[Structure Module and IPA](7-structure-module-and-ipa)** — Invariant point attention, quaternion algebra, and equivariant coordinate generation
- **[Prediction Heads](9-prediction-heads)** — Per-head loss functions, architectures, and configuration patterns

- **[Potts Model and Sequence Design](16-potts-model-and-sequence-design)** — Potts energy functions, MCMC samplers (Gibbs / DLMC), and sequence design workflows

# AlphaFold2 Core Pipeline



This page dissects the end-to-end computational path that transforms raw sequence and structural features into predicted 3D coordinates and auxiliary outputs. ProFOLD2's core pipeline faithfully reimplements the AlphaFold2 architecture while extending it with configurable recycling strategies, a modular header system, and optional frame-based attention mechanisms.

## Pipeline Architecture Overview

The pipeline is organized into four sequential stages — input embedding, recycling injection, the Evoformer trunk, and multi-head prediction — all orchestrated by two primary classes. `AlphaFold2` implements a single forward pass, while `AlphaFold2WithRecycling` wraps it with an iterative recycling loop that progressively refines structural predictions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Input["① Input Embedding"]
        A[InputEmbeddings] --> B["pairwise repr (N×N×c_z)"]
        A --> C["MSA repr (M×N×c_m)"]
        A --> D["MSA mask"]
    end

    subgraph Recycle["② Recycling Injection"]
        R[Recyclables] --> R1["Position distogram → pairwise"]
        R --> R2["Single repr → MSA row 0"]
        R --> R3["Pairwise repr → pairwise"]
        R --> R4["Frames (q, t)"]
    end

    B --> P{Recyclables present?}
    R1 & R2 & R3 --> P
    P -->|Yes| E["Enhanced representations"]
    P -->|No| E

    subgraph Trunk["③ Evoformer Trunk"]
        E --> F["Evoformer (48 layers)"]
        F --> G["pairwise repr x"]
        F --> H["MSA repr m"]
        F --> I["frames t"]
    end

    subgraph Extract["④ Single Extraction"]
        H --> J["to_single_repr (Linear)"]
        J --> K["single repr s"]
    end

    subgraph Heads["⑤ Multi-Head Prediction"]
        K --> L[HeaderBuilder]
        G --> L
        I --> L
        L --> L1[FoldingHead]
        L --> L2[DistogramHead]
        L --> L3[PLDDTHead]
        L --> L4[PAEHead]
        L --> L5[ConfidenceHead]
        L --> L6["...other heads"]
    end

    subgraph Loss["⑥ Loss Computation"]
        L1 --> LT[Weighted Sum]
        L2 --> LT
        L3 --> LT
        L4 --> LT
        L5 --> LT
        LT --> LOSS["Total Loss"]
    end

    subgraph RecycleOut["⑦ Recycling Output"]
        K --> RC1[msa_first_row_repr]
        G --> RC2[pairwise_repr]
        L1 --> RC3[coords]
        I --> RC4[frames]
        RC1 & RC2 & RC3 & RC4 --> R
    end
```

## The Two Model Classes

ProFOLD2 splits the pipeline into a composable inner model and a recycling-aware outer wrapper. This separation allows `AlphaFold2` to be invoked in isolation for feature extraction or single-pass inference, while `AlphaFold2WithRecycling` manages the full iterative protocol used during both training and prediction.

`AlphaFold2` ([alphafold2.py#L128-L320](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L128-L320)) accepts a rich set of configuration parameters. The most architecturally significant are the **dimension tuple** `dim`, which unpacks to `(dim_single, dim_msa, dim_pairwise)`, and the `evoformer_depth` (default 48), which controls the number of trunk iterations. Additional flags such as `accept_frame_attn` and `accept_frame_update` toggle ProFOLD2-specific extensions that inject frame-aware attention into the Evoformer blocks.

`AlphaFold2WithRecycling` ([alphafold2.py#L323-L422](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L323-L422)) delegates all model logic to an inner `AlphaFold2` instance via `self.impl`. Its `forward` method runs a configurable number of recycling iterations (`num_recycle`) under `torch.no_grad()`, then performs a final forward pass with gradient computation and loss evaluation enabled. During training, the actual number of recycling rounds is randomized between 0 and `num_recycle` to regularize the model ([alphafold2.py#L380-L381](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L380-L381)).

Sources: [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L128-L422)

## Stage 1: Input Embeddings

The `InputEmbeddings` module ([alphafold2.py#L62-L125](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L62-L125)) converts raw integer-encoded residue features into dense tensor representations along three parallel tracks: single representation, MSA representation, and pairwise representation.

The **single embedding** uses a standard `nn.Embedding` layer mapping residue types (21 standard amino acids plus an extra token) into the MSA dimension `c_m`. When explicit MSA features are provided via `msa_feat`, a separate linear projection (`to_msa_emb`) maps additional per-position features into the same `c_m` space. When MSA features are absent, the single embedding is broadcast to create a pseudo-MSA of depth 1 — effectively treating the target sequence as its own single-sequence "MSA" ([alphafold2.py#L107-L109](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L107-L109)). In both cases, the single representation is added to the first row of the MSA representation via `tensor_add`, ensuring the target sequence signal is always present at `m[..., 0, :, :]`.

The **pairwise embedding** is constructed by `PairwiseEmbedding` ([commons.py#L1266-L1315](profold2/model/commons.py#L1266-L1315)), which computes a symmetric outer product of single representations and concatenates relative positional encodings. These relative encodings are produced by `RelativePositionEmbedding` ([commons.py#L1180-L1265](profold2/model/commons.py#L1180-L1265)), which operates on sequence indices, chain colors, symmetry groups, and entity IDs — enabling the model to distinguish intra-chain from inter-chain residue pairs in multimer inputs.

| Component | Input Shape | Output Shape | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to_single_emb` | `(..., N)` | `(..., N, c_m)` | Residue type embedding |
| `to_msa_emb` | `(..., M, N, feat)` | `(..., M, N, c_m)` | Optional MSA feature projection |
| `PairwiseEmbedding` | `(..., N, c_m)` | `(..., N, N, c_z)` | Symmetric pairwise features |

Sources: [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L62-L125), [commons.py](profold2/model/commons.py#L1266-L1315)

## Stage 2: Recycling Injection

Recycling is AlphaFold2's mechanism for iterative self-refinement: the model's own predictions from a previous forward pass are fed back as additional input signals. ProFOLD2 implements this through the `Recyclables` dataclass ([alphafold2.py#L24-L37](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L24-L37)), which packages four tensors for cross-iteration communication.

The injection logic ([alphafold2.py#L248-L268](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L248-L268)) merges recyclables into the freshly computed embeddings via additive fusion, each pathway gated by a LayerNorm:

- **Pairwise recycling**: The previous iteration's pairwise representation is normalized and added directly to the new pairwise embeddings.
- **MSA single-row recycling**: The first MSA row receives the previous single representation (optionally projected via `recycling_to_msa_repr` from `dim_single` to `dim_msa`).
- **Position recycling**: When enabled, predicted 3D coordinates are converted to a distance histogram (distogram) via linearly spaced bins from 3.25Å to 20.75Å (15 bins default), then projected into the pairwise dimension and added as a structural prior.

> [!TIP]
> Position recycling converts predicted 3D coordinates into a binned distogram (15 bins spanning 3.25–20.75Å) before injection, not the raw coordinates themselves. This discretization prevents the recycling pathway from memorizing exact coordinate values and instead forces the model to reason about relative distance geometry.

When no recyclables are available (first iteration or no recycling), the `AlphaFold2WithRecycling.forward` method initializes zero-filled tensors of the correct shapes ([alphafold2.py#L373-L378](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L373-L378)). Frame initialization uses identity quaternions `[1, 0, 0, 0]` and zero translations — these "black hole frames" represent an uninformative starting geometry ([alphafold2.py#L264-L268](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L264-L268)).

| Recycling Signal | Condition | Target | Transformation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pairwise_repr` | Always (when recycling) | Pairwise embeddings | LayerNorm → add |
| `msa_first_row_repr` | `recycling_single_repr=True` | MSA row 0 | Optional Linear → LayerNorm → add |
| `coords` | `recycling_pos=True` | Pairwise embeddings | Distogram bins → Linear → add |
| `frames` | `recycling_frames=True` | Evoformer frames | Direct passthrough |

Sources: [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L24-L37), [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L248-L268), [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L373-L378)

## Stage 3: The Evoformer Trunk

With enriched embeddings in hand, the pipeline enters the Evoformer — the central computational engine of the AlphaFold2 architecture. The Evoformer is constructed as a stacked sequence of `EvoformerBlock` modules via `layer_stack` ([evoformer.py#L304-L307](profold2/model/evoformer.py#L304-L307)), repeated `evoformer_depth` times (default 48).

Each `EvoformerBlock` ([evoformer.py#L199-L301](profold2/model/evoformer.py#L199-L301)) performs four distinct operations in sequence, operating on the MSA representation `m`, pairwise representation `x`, and optionally the frame representation `t`:

1. **MSA attention** (`msa_attn`): Row-wise and column-wise attention over the MSA, bias-injected by the pairwise representation. Controlled by `accept_msa_attn` flag.
2. **Frame attention** (`frame_attn`, optional): Invariant Point Attention operating on the first MSA row, using frame quaternions and translations for SE(3)-equivariant geometry reasoning. Enabled by `accept_frame_attn`.
3. **Frame update** (`frame_update`, optional): Directly updates quaternions and translations based on the first MSA row. Enabled by `accept_frame_update`.
4. **Pairwise attention** (`pair_attn`): Triangle multiplication and attention over the pairwise matrix, with outer product mean from the MSA providing an additional update pathway.

The block's forward pass always executes pairwise attention as the final operation, ensuring the pairwise representation receives information from all active pathways before being passed to the next layer. Profiling instrumentation wraps each sub-operation for performance monitoring ([evoformer.py#L262-L299](profold2/model/evoformer.py#L262-L299)).

After the trunk completes, the MSA representation's first row `m[..., 0, :, :]` is extracted and projected to the single representation dimension via `to_single_repr`, a single linear layer ([alphafold2.py#L277](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L277)). This `single` representation becomes the primary input to all downstream prediction heads.

> [!TIP]
> The Evoformer interleaves MSA-space and pairwise-space operations rather than processing them in isolation. The outer product mean in `PairwiseAttentionBlock` compresses MSA information into pairwise updates, while pairwise bias injection in `MsaAttentionBlock` propagates structural signals back into the MSA. This cross-pollination is the core architectural innovation that enables joint reasoning about co-evolution and 3D geometry.

The full forward signature is `forward(self, x, m, t, mask=None, msa_mask=None, shard_size=None)`, returning updated `(x, m, t)` where `x` is pairwise, `m` is MSA, and `t` is the frame tuple `(quaternions, translations)`.

Sources: [evoformer.py](profold2/model/evoformer.py#L199-L307), [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L169-L184), [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L272-L277)

## Stage 4: Multi-Head Prediction

The final stage leverages the `HeaderBuilder` system to invoke a configurable set of prediction heads. Each head consumes some combination of the `single`, `pair`, `msa`, and `frames` representations from the Evoformer trunk and produces both predictions and (during training) loss values.

The header invocation loop ([alphafold2.py#L284-L305](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L284-L305)) iterates over registered `(name, module, options)` tuples. Each head receives the accumulated `headers` dict (allowing heads to reference prior heads' outputs), the `representations` dict, and the raw `batch`. A head may also inject new representations back into the `representations` dict via its return value. After all forward passes, the loop re-enters each head's `loss` method and accumulates a weighted total loss.

The following table summarizes the key heads relevant to the core structure prediction pipeline:

| Head | Input Representation | Output | Loss |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FoldingHead` | single + pair + frames | 3D coordinates, frames | FAPE structural loss |
| `DistogramHead` | pair | Distance histogram logits | Cross-entropy on binned distances |
| `PLDDTHead` | single | Per-residue confidence | Cross-entropy on binned lDDT |
| `PAEHead` | single + pair | Predicted alignment error | Cross-entropy on binned PAE |
| `ConfidenceHead` | (computed from lDDT/PAE) | pLDDT, PTM, iPTM metrics | (metric only, no trainable loss) |
| `TMscoreHead` | single + folding coords | Predicted TM-score | MSE against true TM-score |

The `FoldingHead` ([head.py#L403-L694](profold2/model/head.py#L403-L694)) is architecturally the most complex: it wraps the `StructureModule` from [folding.py](profold2/model/folding.py), which iteratively applies Invariant Point Attention (IPA) blocks to refine backbone frames, then predicts torsion angles via `AngleNet` and reconstructs all-atom coordinates through rigid body transformations. Notably, the structure module forces float32 precision for SE(3) equivariance and detaches rotation gradients between iterations for training stability ([folding.py#L147-L190](profold2/model/folding.py#L147-L190)).

After the `FoldingHead` produces coordinates, the pipeline applies `multi_chain_permutation_alignment` ([alphafold2.py#L293](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L293)) to handle chain ordering ambiguity — a critical step for multimer prediction that is explored further in [Multi-Chain and Multimer Handling](15-multi-chain-and-multimer-handling).

Sources: [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L284-L305), [head.py](profold2/model/head.py#L403-L694), [folding.py](profold2/model/folding.py#L99-L213)

## Stage 5: Recycling Output Preparation

When `return_recyclables=True`, the pipeline prepares a `Recyclables` package from the current forward pass for the next recycling iteration ([alphafold2.py#L307-L318](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L307-L318)). This involves selective extraction and optional transformation:

- `msa_first_row_repr`: Taken from `m[..., 0, :, :]` (the target sequence row), optionally projected from `dim_single` to `dim_msa` via `recycling_to_msa_repr`.
- `pairwise_repr`: Taken directly from `representations['pair']` (the final pairwise output of the Evoformer).
- `coords`: Extracted from the `FoldingHead` output if available, otherwise `None`.
- `frames`: Passed through if `recycling_frames` is enabled, otherwise `None`.

Both `msa_first_row_repr` and `pairwise_repr` are detached from the computation graph (`torch.detach`) before packaging, ensuring that recycling iterations do not accumulate gradients across rounds. This is critical: the recycling loop in `AlphaFold2WithRecycling` runs under `torch.no_grad()`, and only the final iteration computes gradients for backpropagation.

The complete forward return value is serialized via `ReturnValues.asdict()` ([alphafold2.py#L53-L59](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L53-L59)), which converts the `Recyclables` dataclass to a plain dict alongside the computed `headers` and `loss`.

Sources: [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L307-L318), [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L365-L398)

## Configuration Parameters Summary

The `AlphaFold2.__init__` method exposes a comprehensive set of hyperparameters. The following table documents the most impactful ones:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dim` | *(required)* | Tuple `(dim_single, dim_msa, dim_pairwise)` defining channel widths |
| `evoformer_depth` | `48` | Number of Evoformer blocks in the trunk |
| `evoformer_head_num` | `8` | Attention heads (or `[msa_heads, pair_heads]` list) |
| `evoformer_head_dim` | `32` | Per-head dimension (or `[msa_dim, pair_dim]` list) |
| `relative_pos_r_max` | `32` | Max residue separation for relative position encoding |
| `recycling_single_repr` | `True` | Enable single repr → MSA recycling pathway |
| `recycling_pos` | `False` | Enable coordinate distogram recycling |
| `recycling_frames` | `False` | Enable frame passthrough recycling |
| `accept_frame_attn` | `False` | Enable IPA-based frame attention in Evoformer |
| `accept_frame_update` | `False` | Enable direct frame updates in Evoformer |
| `headers` | `None` | Dict of header configurations for `HeaderBuilder` |

Sources: [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L131-L154)

This page covered the end-to-end flow from raw features to predicted structures. The following pages examine individual components in depth:

- **[Evoformer and Pairformer Blocks](6-evoformer-and-pairformer-blocks)** — Detailed analysis of the attention mechanisms, triangle operations, and outer product mean that power each trunk iteration.

# Evoformer and Pairformer Blocks



The Evoformer and Pairformer are the computational engines that transform raw sequence and structural embeddings into the rich internal representations used for structure prediction. While they share a common architectural DNA rooted in triangular pair geometry, they differ fundamentally in how they handle the multiple sequence alignment dimension — a distinction that separates the AlphaFold2 lineage from the AlphaFold3-style approach implemented in ProFOLD2. This page dissects both architectures from the inside out, tracing data flow through each sub-module and explaining the key design decisions that govern their behavior.

## Architectural Context

Both the Evoformer and Pairformer sit inside the main `AlphaFold2` module trunk, executed after input embeddings are computed and before prediction heads consume the representations [alphafold2.py](profold2/model/alphafold2.py#L271-L275). The Evoformer operates on a 4D MSA tensor and a 3D pairwise tensor simultaneously, while the Pairformer replaces the MSA dimension with a compact single representation, yielding a lighter architecture suited for scenarios without deep MSA data.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "AlphaFold2 Trunk"
        IE[Input Embeddings] --> EVO[Evoformer Stack]
        EVO --> TSR[To Single Repr]
        TSR --> HEADS[Prediction Heads]
        
        subgraph "EvoformerBlock (×48)"
            MA[MsaAttentionBlock] --> MFF[Msa FeedForward]
            PA[PairwiseAttentionBlock] --> PFF[Pair FeedForward]
        end
    end
    
    subgraph "PairformerBlock (AF3-style)"
        PAB[PairwiseAttnBlock] --> PABFF[Pair SwiGLU FF]
        SPB[SeqAttn via AttentionPairBias] --> SPBFF[Seq SwiGLU FF]
    end

    style EVO fill:#e1f5fe
    style PA fill:#fff3e0
    style MA fill:#e8f5e9
```

## The Evoformer Block

The `EvoformerBlock` is the fundamental repeating unit of the AlphaFold2 trunk, defined as a PyTorch module in [evoformer.py](profold2/model/evoformer.py#L199-L301). Each block receives three tensors — the pairwise representation `x` of shape `(batch, N, N, dim_pairwise)`, the MSA representation `m` of shape `(batch, M, N, dim_msa)`, and an optional frame tuple `t` — and returns updated versions of all three. The block's internal execution follows a strict ordering: MSA attention first, then frame attention (if enabled), then frame update (if enabled), and finally pairwise attention. This ordering matters because pairwise attention consumes the updated MSA representation through the OuterProductMean pathway.

### Configuration Parameters

Each `EvoformerBlock` accepts a rich set of configuration flags that control which sub-modules are instantiated:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|---------|
| `dim_msa` | int | — | Channel dimension of the MSA representation |
| `dim_pairwise` | int | — | Channel dimension of the pairwise representation |
| `heads` | int / list | 8 | Attention heads; supports per-stream via list of length 2 |
| `dim_head` | int / list | 32 | Per-head dimension; supports per-stream via list of length 2 |
| `global_column_attn` | bool | False | Enable global query attention on the MSA column dimension |
| `accept_msa_attn` | bool | True | Instantiate MSA attention and transition blocks |
